TRICK: AIM without Money (Manipur is not included) · Schedule 7: 3 lists containing subject in which Union and States can make laws. (Federal Provisions)
Union list, State list, Concurrent list

Union List Subjects: Initially 97, presently 100 subjects (Defence, arms and ammunition, atomic energy, citizenship, airways, inter-state trade and commerce, banking, foreign affairs, labour and mines, census, etc.)
State List Subjects: Initially 66, presently 61 subjects.
(Public order, local government, Health, pilgrimage, liquor, agriculture, fisheries, betting and gambling, Co-operative societies, Land, Lotteries).
Five scenarios in which Parliament/Union can legislate on State list subjects- 1) National Emergency (Article 250): Law valid 6 months after emergency ends.
2) President's Rule (Article 356): Law continues until repealed/amended later or if LS passes a resolution through Simple Majority.
3) If two or more state legislature requests (Article 252):
Permanent until repealed by parliament, states cannot amend it themselves.
4) To enforce international treaty (Article 253).
5) If Rajya Sabha gives Parliament this power (by special majority) in National Interest (Article 249): A resolution thus passed is valid for one year +6 months after expiry.
Concurrent List Subjects: Initially 47, presently 52 subjects.

Both State and Centre can make laws on subjects given in this list. But if both make law Centre's law will prevail over States' law. States' law can prevail only in 1 case when the States' Bill is given assent by President. (Marriage and divorce, criminal laws, code of criminal procedure, insolvency and bankruptcy, trade and labour disputes, electricity, education, weights and measures, etc.)
Parliament can later nullify such a state law by passing another law on the same subject.
Residuary List:
These subjects are not included in Union/State/Concurrent list.
Parliament has the power to legislate on residuary subjects.
Subjects Transferred through 42nd Amendment (From State list to Concurrent list):
Protection of wild animals and birds
